title: Myth and memory: The Lemko path from displacement to renewal
abstract: How does remembering forced displacement become a means of protecting collective identity? Drawing on ethnographic research and published testimonies concerning the Lemkos in Poland, this article develops the Trauma-Myth-Mnemonic Security model. It distinguishes historical rupture, the symbolisation of collective harm, mythic stabilisation and protective mobilisation as overlapping, contingent processes. Building on Mälksoo’s concept of mnemonical security, Trauma-Myth-Mnemonic Security explains how foundational narratives become resources for sustaining belonging and interpretive sovereignty under conditions of dispersion and unequal narrative power. The analysis traces this mechanism through displacement testimonies, representations of homeland, cultural gatherings, community collections and renewed access to religious sites. It argues that memory’s protective capacity depends on practices connecting durable meanings to opportunities for transmission and participation. Preserving heritage does not necessarily preserve these relationships. Mnemonic security emerges where actors mobilise remembered loss to sustain the social and interpretive conditions of collective continuity, through minority initiatives and cooperation beyond the group.
